items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I worked up on the North Side with a guy named Spider.

ctx.x: Yeah. And I couldn't gig around because I was buying (inaudible) and dropped my local Chicago card -- I was 802, behind me about 6 months in my dues, 208 and they wouldn't let me work, and I had some gigs around town I could have worked. I worked up on the North Side with a guy named Spider. Spider was the drummer out of Pittsburgh that was playing at a little club called the French Poodle up near the North Side. And he had Dodo Marmarosa Mamarosa in tow. Dodo was playing piano, I was playing bass and Spider was…

drums. In come the delegate. 'Boy, you know you ain't supposed to be on that bandstand.' And I said, 'Man, well, how do you expect me to make it then?' -- and blah, blah, blah. He was gonna have me up before the Board, and I went down there, and I went off; I screamed, and they wound up getting me fined. I had to pay a fine to the International for cussing them out. Grey was the President of the black local. You know, it was just a thing with them; I had to kiss their ass in order to work, you know, and I had…
